item.title: Opposition parties Pro and Volt team up to force budget deal
item.description:
Opposition parties Pro and Volt team up to force budget deal

September 26, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Opposition parties Pro and Volt have joined forces for the next round of budget negotiations as they try to step up the pressure on the cabinet to make further concessions on social security.

Prime minister Rob Jetten said ministers had spent the last week drawing up “a new and attractive offer” addressing opposition parties’ concerns on welfare, the cost of living and replacing the “Box 3” asset tax mechanism.

Pro leader Jesse Klaver said the combined votes of his left-wing party and the pro-European Volt would give the government a “stable majority” in both houses of parliament.

An agreement with both Pro and Volt would give the coalition parties a comfortable majority in the lower house and the 16 seats it needs in the Senate, where Pro is the largest group but still needs Volt’s two seats to get over the line.

But the right-wing liberal VVD, the party of finance minister Eelco Heinen, is anxious not to make too many concessions to Pro, which would risk driving its voters away to its rivals such as JA21 and Geert Wilders’ far-right PVV.

Pick a side

“We are fighting for progress for ordinary people and a fair contribution from the super-rich,” Klaver said. “We believe in progressive co-operation.”

Volt leader Laurens Dassen said: “The world is changing rapidly. People expect politicians to work together towards a sustainable and innovative future.”

Jetten has been under pressure from the opposition on left and right to choose a side after all parties poured cold water on his hopes of finding a route through the middle.

The prime minister argued he would be “short-changing the country” if he excluded one side from the talks, but JA21 leader Joost Eerdmans said a broad approach “isn’t going to work” while Klaver warned his party would block the entire budget if the cabinet tried to do separate deals for each department.

Welfare cuts

Heinen has already agreed to postpone or cancel around half of the €6 billion cuts to welfare spending that were in the coalition agreement in February, but Pro wants the cabinet to go further.

Parties such as JA21, on the other hand, want to see even bigger welfare cuts, arguing that lower taxes are the best way to relieve the pressure on households and businesses.

Jetten and Heinen held talks on Saturday with Pro, Volt and the ChristenUnie, whose leader, Mirjam Bikker, said there had been “movement” from the coalition parties.

The ChristenUnie’s priorities are to ensure households are able to pay for essentials through the winter as energy and grocery bills rise. Bikker said it was “high time” that the coalition parties “feel the urgency” to make a deal.

BBB back on board

Later on Saturday the two ministers are due to talk to JA21 and the orthodox-protestant SGP, who have formed a right-wing alliance with 12 seats in the lower house.

Jetten and Heinen will also speak to Jan Struijs, leader of pensioners’ party 50Plus, and Henk Vermeer of the farmers’ party BBB, who are the second largest party in the Senate.

Jetten had initially said the BBB were no longer an option after the party backed a motion of no confidence during the budget debate, but he and Vermeer patched up their differences in a phone call last week.

item.title: Man shot dead in packed bar in Amsterdam was prison warden
item.description:
Man shot dead in packed bar in Amsterdam was prison warden

September 26, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

A man who was shot dead on a packed terrace in Amsterdam on Friday afternoon was a warden at a local prison, Dutch media have confirmed.

Marcel Blijd was killed at point-blank range as he sat outside De Baanderij restaurant on the NSDM quay, on the north bank of the IJ, in what initially appeared to be a row over a dog running off its leash.

Sources quoted by Het Parool and local crime news sites said the gunman had previously been detained in Zaandstad prison, where Blijd worked, but it is not clear if the two men knew each other.

The shooting at 3pm was witnessed by dozens of people who were enjoying a drink at the bar, and filmed by several people in the area.

Video footage showed the gunman, wearing a white shirt and red trousers, threw the weapon into the water but made no effort to flee and surrendered to police when they arrived a few minutes later.


One witness said the two men clashed initially over the shooter’s dog, which was running loose around the quayside and barking. “He walked up and down a few times. We thought they were going to come to blows, but then there were shots.”

An ambulance and air ambulance were called to the scene, but Blijd could not be saved. A child’s buggy was parked next to the spot where he lay.

Detectives are now investigating whether the shooting was linked to Blijd’s position at Zaanstad jail, where some of Amsterdam’s most dangerous criminals are housed, including members of the Top 600 – a list of repeat offenders, many with connections to the underworld.

“Father figure”

Blijd worked in the prison system for 30 years and was seen as a “father figure” by colleagues and the young criminals he worked with, one colleague told Het Parool.

“Marcel could get on with everybody,” the colleague said. “If you were working with him in the cell block, you knew it was going to be a good day.”

Police cordoned off the area around the terrace and ferries to and from Amsterdam Centraal Station, which dock beside the restaurant, were suspended for three hours while investigations were carried out at the scene.

Witnesses were taken in police vans to the local police station to have their statements taken. Anyone who was in the area at the time can contact Victim Support Netherlands (Slachtofferhulp) for advice and counselling.

item.title: New group home for psychiatric patients tried in Rotterdam
item.description:
New group home for psychiatric patients tried in Rotterdam

September 25, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Rotterdam is to set up a new type of supervised accommodation for homeless people with serious psychiatric problems and addiction issues.

Forty people will be brought together under one roof in Poortugaal, a village near Rotterdam that is also home to a forensic psychiatric clinic, in a supervised environment where they can receive more structured support.

The residents will be allowed to stay in the facility for up to eight years, receiving long-term and structured support that is often lacking in temporary accommodation.

Around 1,500 people in the Netherlands are classed as posing a high risk to public safety. They often have learning difficulties, suffer from psychiatric illness and struggle with addiction, which can lead to aggressive, disruptive or deranged behaviour in public.

Many of the patients have spent their lives alternating between living on the streets and being incarcerated in clinics or prisons, posing a danger to themselves and others.

Pillar to post

“They get passed from pillar to post when what they really need is intensive support for several years,” Laura van Goor, of Artes, the organisation running the facility, told Nieuwsuur. “But we don’t have that right now in the Netherlands.”

Psychiatric clinics are intended for short stays of around three months, but patients often end up staying longer to prevent them ending up back on the streets.

But the treatment is short-term and keeping patients in care for longer adds to waiting lists.

Van Goor said the patients would have more freedom to move around on the campus than in smaller-scale facilities, while also benefiting from a more structured regime. They will not be allowed out unsupervised.

Drink and drugs will be formally banned, unlike in temporary housing where usage is usually tolerated. “But it’s not a case of ‘if you use, you’re out,’ Van Good said. “That’s not possible: 95% of them have drug problems.”

item.title: Nearly half of people experience neighborhood nuisance
item.description:
Nearly half of people experience neighborhood nuisance

September 25, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Almost half of Dutch people say that have experience social nuisance in their neighborhood, from noisy neighbors to the drug trade, according to new figures from the Dutch statistics office.

The CBS released its biennial Safety Monitor on Friday, which found that 42% of adults say they dealt with some type of anti-social behaviour near their homes during 2025.

The report looks at crime and safety issues across the country.

The largest number of complaints stem from loitering youth, which make up 26% of the reported problems. Issues with neighbors account for 20% of the concerns.

Overall problems with nuisance have risen in the past few years. Some 14% of people say they have experienced significant social nuisance in their neighborhood, up from 12% in 2021.

Those living in urban areas have the most problems. City residents report nearly four times the number of issues than non-urban dwellers.

item.title: Cabinet wants private companies to pay more towards gas storage
item.description:
Cabinet wants private companies to pay more towards gas storage

September 25, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

The Dutch government wants to make private companies responsible for storing gas for the winter to cut its liabilities as prices on the markets soar.

At the moment the cost of filling the four gas storage facilities in Norg, Grijpskerk, Bergermeer and Alkmaar is met by the government-funded operator Energie Beheer Nederland, but soaring gas prices mean they are facing a €1 billion loss.

Private companies have no commercial incentive to stock up on gas for the winter because prices are currently forecast to drop after the autumn.

Demand has been stoked by the need for European governments to meet EU-set targets to fill their gas reserves by the start of November. The Netherlands last week reduced its target figure from 74% to 64%. The current storage level is 57.5%.

Under EU rules the Dutch government is also not allowed to keep the stored gas it buys for itself, but must export it to other member states who need it, as well as the UK, which has limited gas storage facilities.

The Netherlands’ facilities date from the time when it exported gas from the Slochteren field in Groningen, but since it was forced to end production two years ago because of earthquakes in the northern province it has filled the chambers with imported gas.

LNG imports

The high cost of importing liquefied national gas from the United States, which is the main supplier, have added to the government’s costs.

It wants to pass on the cost to commercial companies such as Essent, Eneco and Vattenfall by making it mandatory for them to build up their own reserves. A similar obligation is in force in Austria.

“At the moment there is virtually no market in the Netherlands for storing gas in the seasonal storage facilities, even though seasonal storage is an essential element of supply guarantee in the portfolio of suppliers’ prospectuses,” the letter, sent from the ministry of economic affairs, said.

“The question is whether the bill should continue to be met by the Dutch taxpayer, or whether supply guarantee can be be ensured through a different mix of measures for a lower cost.”

The weekend forecast is mostly dry and sunny, with a few showers in the north of the country, predicts the Dutch weather service KNMI.

The meteorologic institute says Friday will be sunny and dry, with highs of 20°C in the north up to 25°C in the southwest.

In the evening, some cloud cover will move in and there is a chance of rain in the north.

Tomorrow will see heavily cloud cover and scattered showers, with highs of 17°C in the north up to 23°C in the southeast.

By Saturday evening, it will be dry. Sunday will be sunny with little chance of rain and highs of 21°C.

item.title: Xavi satisfied as Gakpo earns Oranje late draw against Germany
item.description:
Xavi satisfied as Gakpo earns Oranje late draw against Germany

September 25, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

New Dutch national football coach Xavi Hernandez declared himself satisfied with his team’s performance following the 1-1 draw with Germany in Amsterdam.

Cody Gakpo converted a magnificent skewered pass by debutant Ruben van Bommel with a crashing volley in stoppage time to earn Oranje the point their second-half dominance deserved.

“We were a little nervous in the first half, but the second half is the way we want to play,” the Spaniard said after the opening game in the Nations League, his first match since being appointed last month.

Germany took the lead in the 32nd minute when Felix Nmecha pounced on a loose ball in the penalty, but the Dutch were aggrieved that their opponents had played on after Brian Brobbey went down injured in the centre circle.

Captain Virgil van Dijk said: “We thought the ball should have gone out, but it didn’t go out, and it was unfortunate that it fell right in front of them after a good block by Jan Paul van Hecke.”

Van Dijk had the ball in the net after 15 minutes, but his header was disallowed after the referee decided Brobbey had impeded goalkeeper Marc-André ter Stegen.

Zierkzee recall

Brobbey was replaced by AZ striker Mexx Meerdink, who missed a glorious chance to equalise on his debut after Crysencio Summerville made space in the penalty area with a smart turn.

On Friday Xavi called up Manchester United striker Joshua Zirkzee, who last played for the national team two years ago, as a replacement for Brobbey ahead of the next Nations League match against Serbia in Belgrade on Sunday.

Van Bommel, who became the third generation of his family to play for Oranje after and his father, Mark, his grandfather, Bert van Marwijk, came on in the second half and capped his debut with the assist that set up Gakpo’s goal.

“I ran forward and I saw Cody free at the far post, and I thought, I have to get it to him somehow. It wasn’t an easy finish, but the pass wasn’t bad either,” the PSV winger said.

Another second-half substitute was Borussia Dortmund midfielder Joey Veerman, who made his first appearance in an orange shirt for two years after being frozen out of the international set-up by Xavi’s predecessor Ronald Koeman. Veerman came on for Marseille’s Quinten Timber, who was selected to take the place of the injured Frenkie de Jong.

item.title: Dutch PM Jetten warns “hands off the ICC” in debut UN speech
item.description:
Dutch PM Jetten warns “hands off the ICC” in debut UN speech

September 25, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Prime minister Rob Jetten gave a fiery address to the United Nations on Thursday, defending the International Criminal Court and the rule of law.

“Hands off the ICC and all those other institutions that protect the international legal order,” he said in his first address at the UN’s annual meeting in New York.

Although Jetten did not call out American president Donald Trump specifically, the speech came after reporting earlier this week that the United States is planning to escalate its fight with the ICC and sanction the institution as a whole as part of its campaign to dismantle the court “brick by brick”.

The White House has already sanctioned 13 staff members, including court president, Japanese Judge Tomoko Akane, over the investigation into alleged Israeli war crimes in Gaza.

“Take, for example, the attempts to undermine the International Criminal Court – a court based in my country, in my city. This undermines the international legal order as a whole. And that affects us all,” Jetten said.

As the court’s host state, the Netherlands is obliged to provide assistance such as cooperation with security, facilitating visas and transporting defendants and witnesses.

He also called for Russia to be held accountable for the war in Ukraine. “In this conflict, Ukraine has no choice but to defend itself,” said Jetten. “But Russia chooses to wage war day after day,” he said.

item.title: Van Weel survives no-confidence debate over crime stats row
item.description:
Van Weel survives no-confidence debate over crime stats row

September 25, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Justice minister David van Weel has survived a motion of no confidence after he apologised to MPs who accused him of misleading them over police crime figures.

MPs called an emergency debate on Thursday over the minister’s response to reports that police had not responded to some 10,000 criminal complaints because they lacked the capacity to do so.

Van Weel told parliament in June that more than half the cases were reports of crimes rather than official complaints, which police are required to investigate.

But he was corrected by the government’s audit office, the Algemene Rekenkamer, which said in its annual report to parliament that only 10% of the cited cases were verbal reports.

“The consequence is that victims of crimes such as sexual offences and serious theft had not had justice and these serious cases have not had any significant attention,” the auditors wrote.

Van Weel initially tried to shrug off the reprimand as a “difference of insight”, but after MPs called a debate and tabled a motion of no confidence he attempted to apologise for his choice of words.

Measures of crime

The minister blamed the confusion on the different criteria used to measure the seriousness of the complaint. Police prioritise crimes based on how much evidence is available to start an investigation, such as witness statements and camera footage, while auditors use the “Crime Harm Index”, which looks at the severity of sentences imposed by courts.

Van Weel acknowledged that he had “given the impression” that he “had trivialised the seriousness of the Court of Audit’s report”, but insisted: “That doesn’t make it wrong information.

Opposition MPs said the minister’s explanation did not go far enough and threatened to back a motion of no confidence tabled by the far-right PVV, which would have forced Van Weel to resign.

Different attitude

“The minister has had several chances to say he gave parliament the wrong impression, but hasn’t taken them,” said Caroline van der Plas of the farmers’ party BBB.

Van Weel made a second, stronger apology that stopped short of admitting he had misled MPs, which was enough to persuade all parties not to vote for the motion, with the exception of the PVV and Forum voor Democratie.

“I realise now, after your contributions, that I intentionally or unintentionally gave you the wrong impression and that you felt misled,” he said. “That was never my intention, but it shouldn’t have happened.”

“At the last minute we saw a different attitude,” Ingrid Coenradie of right-wing opposition party JA21 commented. “We would have liked to have seen that at the start.”
